# AI slop checker: find the signs of AI writing

The signs of AI writing this checker finds are filler phrases, contrastive negation, hedging, unsourced numbers, stock closings and the monotone rhythm of sentences cut to one length. Each one is a named rule with a fix.

Paste a draft. You get back the sentences that read as generated, the rule each one broke, and the fix. The rules are the ones that gate every article seodraft ships, run over your text alone.

## What AI slop is

AI slop is text whose sentences are individually correct and collectively empty: a filler opener, a contrast that denies what nobody believed, a hedge on every claim the writer did not measure, a statistic with no owner, and a closing line that restates the paragraph. Most of that shape has a grammar, which is what lets code find it.

The rules came from a count. Over the eleven articles published from this repository, the contrastive negation alone appeared between 0 and 5 times per article, and eight of the eleven carried two or more.

## How the checker works

Ten rules are deterministic: they read sentences, headings, paragraphs and lists, and return the same answer for the same text every time. Two more come from a classifier that reads meaning, and those two only advise. The same code runs inside seodraft as the editorial gate. Nothing on this page rewrites your text.

## The twelve rules

Each rule has a name, a definition, the measurement behind it, and the fix as steps. Use the name when you brief an agent.

### Contrastive negation

Blocks in the gate · Deterministic

Definition

A contrastive negation affirms one thing by denying another: "X, not Y", "it is not X, it is Y", "not just X but Y", or the same figure split over two sentences. The rule counts them across the prose, the title, the summary and the H2s, and allows one per article.

Measured

Measured over the eleven articles published from this repository, the shape appeared between 0 and 5 times per article, and eight of the eleven carried two or more.

Fix

Delete the negated half and read the sentence again. If the shorter sentence says the same thing, keep it shorter. Keep the contrast only where the reader believes the thing you are denying, and name that belief with its number.

Fails

The problem is not the prompt, it is the inputs. It is not about writing more, it is about writing what nobody else measured.

Passes

The problem is the inputs: the draft cites three industry figures and none of ours.

### Filler phrases

A filler phrase is a fixed expression that occupies a sentence without adding a fact: "in today's digital landscape", "it's important to note", "delve into", "game-changer", "en la era digital", "cabe destacar", "sin duda". The rule matches a bilingual list of 57 of them across the body, the title and the summary, and any hit fails.

Each entry has a spelling, so a string comparison finds it every time. The list carries 27 Spanish entries and 30 English ones, and a text in either language is read against both.

Delete the phrase. If the sentence still stands, you are done. If it collapses, delete the sentence.

In today's digital landscape, it's important to note that email deliverability is a game-changer for any startup.

Of the 1,240 emails we sent in March, 71 bounced.

### Hedging

Advisory · Deterministic

Hedging softens a claim with "might", "perhaps", "somewhat", "arguably", "tends to be", "quizás", "probablemente" or "suele ser". The rule counts 15 such phrases over the prose and advises when they exceed 8 per 1,000 words.

The ceiling is a rate rather than a count, so a 2,000-word article can hedge sixteen times before it fires. Below that it stays quiet.

For each hedge, write down what you would need to know to remove it. If you know it, state it with the number. If you do not, say what you measured and stop.

This could potentially reduce bounce rates somewhat, and it might arguably be worth trying in some cases.

Cleaning the list cut the bounce rate from 5.7% to 0.9% on the next send.

### Answer first

Blocks in the gate · Deterministic · Needs H2 headings

Answer first means the opening sentence under every H2 carries the answer to that heading on its own: at least six words, never a question, and never one of 43 openers that postpone the answer, such as "as we saw", "before we begin", "it depends" or "there are many ways".

The first sentence under a heading is the passage an answer engine extracts. The six-word floor is what keeps a one-word answer from passing.

Write the answer as one complete sentence. Use the rest of the section to qualify it. If the honest answer is a condition, put the condition and the outcome in the same sentence.

## How long does the trial last? Before we get into that, there are a few things worth understanding about how billing works.

## How long does the trial last? The trial lasts seven days from signup and ends without a charge if you cancel before day seven.

### Intro length

The intro is every prose sentence before the first H2. The rule requires between 3 and 14 of them: a preview of the answer, one piece of proof, a preview of the structure and a transition.

Three is the smallest count that fits an answer, a proof and a transition. Across the twelve documents in this repository, intros run from 2 to 9 sentences.

Open with the answer in one sentence. Follow it with the number or case that proves it. Say what the sections cover. Start the first H2.

Email deliverability matters. ## What is deliverability

Seventy-one of the 1,240 emails we sent in March bounced, and every one came from a list we had not cleaned in a year. This article shows what we changed, in order, with the bounce rate after each step. Start with the list, because that is where 90% of the damage was. ## What is deliverability

### Generic closing

A generic closing is a last H2 titled "Conclusion", "Final thoughts", "Summary", "Wrapping up", "Conclusiones" or "Reflexiones finales". The rule checks the last heading against 13 of these and fails on a match.

The rule reads the last H2 only, so a section with one of these titles in the middle of an article passes.

Name the decision the reader has to make now. Give the next step and one resource for it. If there is no decision and no next step, delete the section.

## Conclusion In summary, deliverability is a complex topic with many factors to consider.

## Clean the list before you touch the template Run the bounce report for the last 90 days and remove every address that bounced twice. Then send the next campaign and compare.

### Sentence variety

Sentence variety measures how much sentence length moves across a text. Over 15 or more sentences, the rule computes the standard deviation of words per sentence and advises when it falls under 4.

Across the twelve documents in this repository the deviation runs from 4.4 to 9.6 words. The threshold of 4 sits under the lowest of them.

Find three consecutive sentences of the same length. Cut one to under eight words. Let another run past twenty-five if it has two clauses that belong together.

We cleaned the list in March. We changed the sender domain in April. We rewrote the template in May. We measured the bounce rate in June.

We cleaned the list in March. April was the sender domain, which took two weeks of DNS changes and one support ticket nobody answered. The template came in May.

### Paragraph length

Paragraph length counts the sentences in each prose paragraph and advises when any paragraph runs past four. Lists, headings, tables and code are skipped.

Eight of the twelve documents in this repository keep every paragraph at four sentences or fewer. The advisory names the longest paragraph it found.

Find the sentence where the subject changes and break the paragraph there. If no sentence changes the subject, the extra sentences repeat the first one, so delete them.

The list had 1,240 addresses. We had not cleaned it in a year. Seventy-one bounced in March. The sender domain was also new. It had no reputation yet. Both problems hit the same campaign.

The list had 1,240 addresses and we had not cleaned it in a year. Seventy-one bounced in March. The sender domain was also new, with no reputation yet. Both problems hit the same campaign.

### Bold-label lists

A bold-label list is a bullet list where each item opens with a bold label and a colon: "**Speed**: the fastest option". The rule counts bullets in that shape and advises when they exceed 70% of a list with four or more items.

The shape is the default output of a model asked for key points. The 70% line lets a list keep one or two labelled items among plain ones.

Keep one list in that shape if the labels are real categories. Turn the others into prose, or into a table if every item has the same two or three attributes.

- **Speed**: the fastest option we tested - **Cost**: the cheapest per send - **Support**: answered in under an hour - **Docs**: complete and current

It was the fastest option we tested and the cheapest per send. Support answered in under an hour, and the docs covered every endpoint we called.

### Thin content

Advisory · Deterministic · Needs H2 headings

Thin content is an article whose prose, with code blocks and headings removed, runs under 900 words. The rule counts the words and advises below that line.

The threshold is editorial and the rule advises only. The twelve documents in this repository run from 517 to 1,364 words, and two of them sit under 900.

Add the measurement, the case or the mistake that is missing. If you have nothing to add, the article is finished.

A 480-word article with three H2s and no numbers.

The same article with a table of the bounce rate after each of the four changes.

### Straw-man contrast

Advisory · Classifier

A straw-man contrast is a contrastive negation whose negated half nobody held. A classifier reads the article and returns the probability that at least one contrast is of this kind. Above 0.6 the tool advises.

The question scored 0.90 on an article whose contrasts deny nobody, against 0.43, 0.50 and 0.55 on three articles from this repository whose contrasts name a real belief. The 0.6 threshold sits in that gap.

For each contrast, write down who believes the negated half and what number they would quote. If you cannot name them, delete the negated half. If you can, put their number in the sentence.

Deliverability is about reputation, not about luck.

Deliverability is about reputation. The four founders we talked to blamed the template first, and the template was the last of four things that moved the number.

### Unsourced numbers

An unsourced number is a statistic with no owner: "studies show 73% of users", "most companies see a 3x lift". A classifier reads the article and returns the probability that its figures are first-hand measurements or named cases. Below 0.35 the tool advises.

Three numbers with no owner satisfy every rule that counts evidence. A draft engineered to pass the whole deterministic standard on invented statistics scored 0.04 on this question, where this repository's reference article scores 0.90.

For each figure, name who measured it and when, or replace it with a figure you measured. Delete a figure you can do neither with.

Studies show that 73% of marketing emails are never opened, and most companies see a 3x lift after cleaning their list.

Of the 1,240 emails we sent in March, 412 were opened. After cleaning the list, the April send reached 1,098 addresses and 468 opened.

## What it does not flag

- A concessive contrast passes the checker with no finding. "Retrying did not recover the screen, but a reload did" is a fact from one of seodraft's own articles, and a rule that fails an article for reporting a fact gets worked around.
